bull_bear.body:
- Integrated design, engineering, manufacturing and erection capability for PEB systems, enabling delivery of complete building solutions rather than components
- Stated record of on-time project delivery — 'We are known for delivering projects on time, every time, even under challenging site conditions and stringent deadlines'
- Full suite of management-system certifications (ISO 9001/14001/45001, IMS) plus ZED Gold, supporting credibility with customers and partners
- Ability to extend existing roll-formed steel expertise into adjacent products (solar module mounting structures, insulated panels) without a new technology base
- In-house technology upgrades — state-of-the-art H-beam automatic welding and plasma cutting machines producing defect-free welds and faster processing than manual welding
- Repeat business from industry leaders and global corporations on the basis of time, quality and cost
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- No formal enterprise risk-management body at board level — The Directors' Report states the Company is not required to constitute a Risk Management Committee under the SEBI Listing Regulations, and none is reported as constituted. Risk oversight therefore rests on the general board and audit-committee process rather than a dedicated risk function — a structural governance gap as the Company scales into new products and larger projects. Verbatim: 'The Company is not required to constitute Risk Management Committee as provided in the SEBI (Listing Obligations & Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.'
- Internal financial controls are sized to a small company, not to the expanded one — Controls are described only as 'commensurate the size, scale and complexity of its operations' and as an integrated part of the risk-management process. With revenue growing sharply and two new lines being added, a control framework calibrated to the prior scale is a risk in itself; the report offers no description of controls being strengthened for the larger footprint.
- Project-execution dependence — revenue is driven by project execution rather than recurring offtake — Management attributes the year's performance to 'higher execution of projects, improved manufacturing capacity utilisation, and increased business across the Company's product portfolio'. Earnings therefore turn on winning and executing discrete projects; a slowdown in order flow or site-level delays translates directly into revenue, and the report discloses no order book or pipeline to cushion that.
- Execution and ramp risk on the Phase 5, Phase 6 and solar MMS expansions — Phase 5 (approx. 26,000 sq. ft. shot blasting and painting) and Phase 6 (approx. 20,000 sq. ft. light fabrication) were still under construction with a completion expectation of August 2026, and the stated step-up in PEB capacity to approximately 1,200 MT per month is conditional on that completion. The new solar MMS line of approximately 2,000 MT per month was commissioned only in June 2026 and is unproven in operation, so a meaningful part of the capacity story is still forward-looking.
- Entry into a new end-market (solar module mounting structures) with no track record — The MMS line serves the renewable energy sector — a different customer set, tender structure and competitive field from PEB buildings. The Company is leveraging existing roll-formed steel expertise, but it carries no disclosed history in this segment, and the report gives no customer commitments or contracted volumes for the new capacity.
- Capital is being retained for expansion instead of returned, tightening funding of growth — No dividend was declared for FY2025-26 'taking into consideration the resources needed for future expansion plans', indicating the expansion programme is being funded substantially from internal accruals. That leaves limited slack if project costs overrun or the capacity ramp is slower than expected. (The AGM Notice elsewhere in the report proposes a Rs. 1.5 per share final dividend for the same year, so the report is internally inconsistent on this point.)
- Single-entity, single-location structure with no diversification — 'The Company has no Subsidiaries, Joint ventures, or Associates.' All operations sit in one standalone entity at the Savli, Vadodara site, so there is no geographic or corporate diversification to absorb a disruption at that location or a downturn in the domestic construction cycle.
- SME-grade credit standing constrains the cost and scale of external funding — The only rating disclosed is under 'CRISIL SME Grading' — i.e. an SME grading rather than a full corporate credit rating. For a capital-intensive, working-capital-heavy project business expanding its footprint, that limits access to and pricing of debt relative to larger rated peers.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Bansal Roofing Products Limited designs, engineers, manufactures and erects pre-engineered building (PEB) systems, roofing systems and allied products, and also makes heavy steel structures and solar module mounting structures. The integrated design-to-erection capability lets it supply robust, cost-effective and scalable industrial and infrastructure buildings to customers across industries. During the year under review it entered the Solar Module Mounting Structure segment, leveraging its existing roll-formed steel expertise, and took a step into the insulated panels business.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Pre-Engineered Buildings:** Pre-Engineered Buildings (PEBs), Roofing Systems, allied products
- **Heavy steel structures:** heavy steel structures, light fabrication, shot blasting and painting of pre-engineered steel structures
- **Renewable energy:** Solar Module Mounting Structures (MMS)
- **Building envelope:** insulated panels
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Integrated design, engineering, manufacturing and erection capability for PEB systems, enabling delivery of complete building solutions rather than components
- Stated record of on-time project delivery — 'We are known for delivering projects on time, every time, even under challenging site conditions and stringent deadlines'
- Full suite of management-system certifications (ISO 9001/14001/45001, IMS) plus ZED Gold, supporting credibility with customers and partners
- Ability to extend existing roll-formed steel expertise into adjacent products (solar module mounting structures, insulated panels) without a new technology base
- In-house technology upgrades — state-of-the-art H-beam automatic welding and plasma cutting machines producing defect-free welds and faster processing than manual welding
- Repeat business from industry leaders and global corporations on the basis of time, quality and cost
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Stay focused on the integrated model — designing, engineering, manufacturing and erecting pre-engineered building systems — to serve customers across industries with scalable infrastructure
- Diversify into high-growth sectors: entry into the Solar Module Mounting Structure (MMS) segment, leveraging existing roll-formed steel expertise to serve the renewable energy industry
- Broaden the portfolio into insulated panels, to become a comprehensive provider of engineered building solutions
- Continue strengthening manufacturing infrastructure through phased built-up-area expansion (Phase 5 shot blasting and painting, Phase 6 light fabrication) to add finishing capability and PEB capacity
- Retain earnings for expansion rather than distribute — no dividend declared for FY2025-26 'taking into consideration the resources needed for future expansion plans'
- Compete on the combination of time, quality and cost — on-time delivery even under challenging site conditions — to build repeat relationships with industry leaders and global corporations
- Upgrade process technology in-house (H-beam automatic welding, plasma cutting) to raise precision and throughput
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: BRPL continued to build out its Savli (Vadodara) manufacturing footprint through FY2025-26, extending the phased programme begun the previous year. The Phase 5 expansion commenced during the year and was under construction at the report date: approximately 26,000 sq. ft. of additional built-up area being developed primarily for shot blasting and painting of pre-engineered steel structures, to add finishing capability. Construction of Phase 6 was also initiated, comprising an additional 20,000 sq. ft. manufacturing shed for light fabrication activities. Both Phase 5 and Phase 6 were expected to be completed by August 2026, upon which installed PEB manufacturing capacity is expected to rise to approximately 1,200 MT per month (capacity derived considering two shifts of eight hours each and production parameters). Separately, as part of a stated strategy to diversify into high-growth sectors, the Company entered the Solar Module Mounting Structure (MMS) segment by leveraging existing roll-formed steel expertise: orders for advanced high-speed roll forming machinery were placed in December 2025 and successfully commissioned in June 2026, establishing a new line for the renewable energy sector with installed capacity of approximately 2,000 MT per month. Management states these initiatives should strengthen manufacturing capability, improve operational efficiency and diversify revenue streams. No rupee quantum for any of these projects is disclosed in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Revenue growth in the year was driven by higher execution of projects, improved manufacturing capacity utilisation, and increased business across the product portfolio
- Profitability improvement outpaced revenue growth on enhanced operational efficiency, better cost management, improved product mix and operating leverage
- India's acceleration of investment in infrastructure and renewable energy is the demand backdrop management cites for expanding capability
- Rapid infrastructure development, industrial expansion and global manufacturing integration in India are raising demand for speed, precision, quality and sustainability in construction
- India's emergence as a preferred global manufacturing hub significantly heightens demand for rapid, scalable and dependable building solutions
- Solar mounting structures position the company in one of the fastest-growing segments of the renewable energy industry
- Phase 5/Phase 6 completion and the new MMS line are expected to strengthen manufacturing capabilities, improve operational efficiencies and diversify revenue streams
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

risks.risk: No formal enterprise risk-management body at board level
risks.note: The Directors' Report states the Company is not required to constitute a Risk Management Committee under the SEBI Listing Regulations, and none is reported as constituted. Risk oversight therefore rests on the general board and audit-committee process rather than a dedicated risk function — a structural governance gap as the Company scales into new products and larger projects. Verbatim: 'The Company is not required to constitute Risk Management Committee as provided in the SEBI (Listing Obligations & Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.'

risks.risk: Internal financial controls are sized to a small company, not to the expanded one
risks.note: Controls are described only as 'commensurate the size, scale and complexity of its operations' and as an integrated part of the risk-management process. With revenue growing sharply and two new lines being added, a control framework calibrated to the prior scale is a risk in itself; the report offers no description of controls being strengthened for the larger footprint.

risks.risk: Project-execution dependence — revenue is driven by project execution rather than recurring offtake
risks.note: Management attributes the year's performance to 'higher execution of projects, improved manufacturing capacity utilisation, and increased business across the Company's product portfolio'. Earnings therefore turn on winning and executing discrete projects; a slowdown in order flow or site-level delays translates directly into revenue, and the report discloses no order book or pipeline to cushion that.

risks.risk: Execution and ramp risk on the Phase 5, Phase 6 and solar MMS expansions
risks.note: Phase 5 (approx. 26,000 sq. ft. shot blasting and painting) and Phase 6 (approx. 20,000 sq. ft. light fabrication) were still under construction with a completion expectation of August 2026, and the stated step-up in PEB capacity to approximately 1,200 MT per month is conditional on that completion. The new solar MMS line of approximately 2,000 MT per month was commissioned only in June 2026 and is unproven in operation, so a meaningful part of the capacity story is still forward-looking.

risks.risk: Entry into a new end-market (solar module mounting structures) with no track record
risks.note: The MMS line serves the renewable energy sector — a different customer set, tender structure and competitive field from PEB buildings. The Company is leveraging existing roll-formed steel expertise, but it carries no disclosed history in this segment, and the report gives no customer commitments or contracted volumes for the new capacity.

risks.risk: Capital is being retained for expansion instead of returned, tightening funding of growth
risks.note: No dividend was declared for FY2025-26 'taking into consideration the resources needed for future expansion plans', indicating the expansion programme is being funded substantially from internal accruals. That leaves limited slack if project costs overrun or the capacity ramp is slower than expected. (The AGM Notice elsewhere in the report proposes a Rs. 1.5 per share final dividend for the same year, so the report is internally inconsistent on this point.)

risks.risk: Single-entity, single-location structure with no diversification
risks.note: 'The Company has no Subsidiaries, Joint ventures, or Associates.' All operations sit in one standalone entity at the Savli, Vadodara site, so there is no geographic or corporate diversification to absorb a disruption at that location or a downturn in the domestic construction cycle.

risks.risk: SME-grade credit standing constrains the cost and scale of external funding
risks.note: The only rating disclosed is under 'CRISIL SME Grading' — i.e. an SME grading rather than a full corporate credit rating. For a capital-intensive, working-capital-heavy project business expanding its footprint, that limits access to and pricing of debt relative to larger rated peers.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Vadodara-based manufacturer of pre-engineered steel buildings, heavy steel structures and solar module mounting structures, offering integrated design, engineering, manufacturing and erection.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Bansal Roofing Products Limited designs, engineers, manufactures and erects pre-engineered building (PEB) systems, roofing systems and allied products, and also makes heavy steel structures and solar module mounting structures. The integrated design-to-erection capability lets it supply robust, cost-effective and scalable industrial and infrastructure buildings to customers across industries. During the year under review it entered the Solar Module Mounting Structure segment, leveraging its existing roll-formed steel expertise, and took a step into the insulated panels business.

- **Renewable energy:** Solar Module Mounting Structures (MMS)
- **Building envelope:** insulated panels

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Revenue growth in the year was driven by higher execution of projects, improved manufacturing capacity utilisation, and increased business across the product portfolio
- Profitability improvement outpaced revenue growth on enhanced operational efficiency, better cost management, improved product mix and operating leverage
- India's acceleration of investment in infrastructure and renewable energy is the demand backdrop management cites for expanding capability
- Rapid infrastructure development, industrial expansion and global manufacturing integration in India are raising demand for speed, precision, quality and sustainability in construction
- India's emergence as a preferred global manufacturing hub significantly heightens demand for rapid, scalable and dependable building solutions
- Solar mounting structures position the company in one of the fastest-growing segments of the renewable energy industry
- Phase 5/Phase 6 completion and the new MMS line are expected to strengthen manufacturing capabilities, improve operational efficiencies and diversify revenue streams

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Stay focused on the integrated model — designing, engineering, manufacturing and erecting pre-engineered building systems — to serve customers across industries with scalable infrastructure
- Diversify into high-growth sectors: entry into the Solar Module Mounting Structure (MMS) segment, leveraging existing roll-formed steel expertise to serve the renewable energy industry
- Broaden the portfolio into insulated panels, to become a comprehensive provider of engineered building solutions
- Continue strengthening manufacturing infrastructure through phased built-up-area expansion (Phase 5 shot blasting and painting, Phase 6 light fabrication) to add finishing capability and PEB capacity
- Retain earnings for expansion rather than distribute — no dividend declared for FY2025-26 'taking into consideration the resources needed for future expansion plans'
- Compete on the combination of time, quality and cost — on-time delivery even under challenging site conditions — to build repeat relationships with industry leaders and global corporations
- Upgrade process technology in-house (H-beam automatic welding, plasma cutting) to raise precision and throughput

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated design, engineering, manufacturing and erection capability for PEB systems, enabling delivery of complete building solutions rather than components
